comment: Enterprise App Review Agent — Greptile configuration

rules.rule: Flag any hardcoded secrets, API keys, tokens, passwords, or credentials. This is CRITICAL severity. Check for patterns like 'sk-', 'AKIA', 'ghp_', 'Bearer ', and any string that looks like a key or secret assigned to a variable.
Flag any use of eval(), innerHTML, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, document.write(), or Function() constructor. These are security vulnerabilities that enable code injection attacks.

Flag missing input validation and sanitization. All user inputs — form fields, URL parameters, API request bodies — must be validated before use. SQL queries must use parameterized queries, never string concatenation.
Flag any CORS configuration that uses '*' as allowed origin, or any overly permissive Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. Flag missing Content-Security-Policy headers in server configurations.

Flag any localStorage or sessionStorage usage that stores personally identifiable information (PII) such as names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, SSNs, or authentication tokens. Sensitive data should only exist in memory for the active session.

Flag any outbound HTTP requests to third-party APIs, analytics services, tracking pixels, or telemetry endpoints that are not documented in the README or a configuration file. External data transmission must be intentional and documented.
Flag any CDN-loaded scripts that are not from widely trusted sources (cdnjs.cloudflare.com, unpkg.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net, ajax.googleapis.com). Unknown CDN sources are a supply chain risk.

Flag any single file exceeding 300 lines of code. This is a vibe-coding quality signal — AI-generated code often dumps everything into one file. Suggest splitting into modules with clear responsibilities.
Flag any function or method exceeding 50 lines or that handles multiple distinct responsibilities. Each function should do one thing well. Suggest extracting helper functions.
Flag copy-pasted logic — repeated code blocks that differ only in variable names or minor values. Suggest extracting into reusable functions, components, or utility methods.
Flag generic variable names like 'data', 'result', 'temp', 'item', 'val', 'obj', 'arr', 'res', 'x', 'y' when more descriptive names would improve readability. Variable names should convey intent.

Flag console.log, console.debug, console.warn, print(), System.out.println, or Debug.Log statements that appear to be debugging artifacts left in production code. Suggest removing or replacing with a proper logging framework.

Flag commented-out code blocks. AI-generated code often leaves these as artifacts. Dead code should be removed — version control preserves history. A few lines of comments explaining WHY are fine; commented-out code is not.

Flag inconsistent coding patterns within the same file or project: mixing async/await with .then() callbacks, mixing naming conventions (camelCase and snake_case), mixing state management approaches, or mixing component patterns.

Flag hardcoded values that should be configuration: API URLs, port numbers, timeout values, rate limits, feature flags, email addresses, and environment-specific settings. These should be in environment variables or config files.

Flag placeholder or generic error messages like 'Something went wrong', 'An error occurred', 'Error', or 'Failed'. Error messages should be specific and actionable so users know what happened and what to do.
Flag missing error handling. Every async operation, API call, file operation, and database query should have explicit error handling. Check that catch blocks don't silently swallow errors.
Flag missing authentication or authorization checks on API endpoints, route handlers, or server-side functions that modify data or access sensitive resources.
Flag debug or development configurations that should not be in production: DEBUG=true, development mode flags, verbose logging enabled, source maps in production bundles, or test/mock data.

other.content: This repository receives code uploaded by business users via an automated OneDrive-to-GitHub pipeline. Each app is uploaded to its own directory and gets its own branch (review/app-name) and PR. Many of the applications are AI-generated or vibe-coded. Review with extra scrutiny for common AI code generation patterns: monolithic files, copy-paste logic, missing error handling, placeholder messages, and forgotten debug artifacts. The review decision should be clear — is this code safe to deploy to production or not. Only review files in the app directory — do NOT review pipeline infrastructure files.

CRITICAL severity issues that must block merging: hardcoded secrets, code injection vectors (eval/innerHTML), data exfiltration to undocumented external systems, PII stored in localStorage/sessionStorage across sessions, and missing authentication on data-modifying endpoints.

**/*.html.instructions: Pay special attention to inline scripts, external script sources, form actions pointing to external URLs, and meta tags that could leak information.

**/api/**.instructions: Every API endpoint must validate input, authenticate requests, handle errors explicitly, and never expose internal error details to clients.

**/*.sql.instructions: All queries must use parameterized statements. Flag any string concatenation in query construction. Flag any SELECT * usage in production queries.
